The present suit has been instituted on his behalf by his mother and natural guardian. Defendant No.1 is an electricity distribution company; Defendant No.2 is its contractor; and Defendant No.3 is the insurance provider of Defendant No.1. On 30.06.2016, at approximately 1:45 PM, while the plaintiff and his mother were standing on the balcony of their residence, a sudden gust of wind caused an electric current-- transmitted through live, loosely hanging electric wires from the said pole--to come into contact with the iron grill of the balcony. As a result, the grill became electrified, and the plaintiff suffered an electric shock and was consequently electrocuted. 3 The plaintiff's mother, upon witnessing the incident, grasped the wooden door of the balcony with one hand and, with the other, managed to pull the plaintiff away from the electrified grill. However, by that time, the plaintiff had lost consciousness and his mother also sustained a minor electric shock. 4 The plaintiff's maternal grandfather immediately transported both the plaintiff and his mother to Gandhi Hospital, where they were administered medical treatment. The plaintiff's mother was discharged on the same day, while the plaintiff was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) due to serious burn injuries sustained on his right arm and the right side of his head caused by the high voltage current. As the plaintiff's condition continued to deteriorate, he was transferred to PGI Chandigarh for advanced treatment. Ultimately, the severity of the injuries necessitated the amputation of the plaintiff's right arm and disarticulation at the right shoulder. The plaintiff has since been certified as suffering from 94% permanent locomotor disability. He remains under ongoing medical supervision at PGI Chandigarh, requiring regular visits by his mother and other family members. 5 On 30.06.2016, the plaintiff's paternal grandfather contacted the Police Control Room (PCR), following which an Investigating Officer (IO) from PS Uttam Nagar arrived at Gandhi Hospital and recorded the statement of the plaintiff's mother. However, no FIR was registered at that time. Aggrieved thereby, the plaintiff's mother approached the competent Court, resulting in the registration of FIR No. 604/16 on 22.07.2016. 6 During the investigation, the IO arrested two contractors, namely Suman Kumar Das and Mukesh Kumar, based on the statements given by officials of Defendant No.1. It is submitted that Defendant No.1 had entrusted the contract for installation of electric poles and insulation of electric wires to Defendant No.2, a contracting agency. 7 The plaintiff's mother, with financial support from her father, incurred approximately 5,00,000/- towards the plaintiff's medical treatment and related expenses, including frequent travel between Delhi and Chandigarh, accommodation, and other incidental costs. The plaintiff's mother, being a divorcee, had received 3,00,000/- as istridhan and maintenance (covering past, present, and future) from her former husband, which was entirely spent on the plaintiff's medical treatment. Additionally, the plaintiff's maternal grandfather and maternal uncle extended financial assistance by liquidating personal assets including vehicles and household items. However, due to the urgency of the medical treatment and emotional distress, not all medical bills and receipts could be preserved. 8 At the time of the incident, the plaintiff was a student in Class I at Columbia School, Police Line, Vikas Puri, New Delhi, and was performing commendably in academics. However, following the incident, he was compelled to discontinue his education based on medical advice, as the risk of infection to his head injury rendered school attendance unsafe. 9 It is submitted that the incident occurred due to the gross negligence and dereliction of duty on the part of the defendants.
